utterance:
Samuel, I've felt your tummy and done some basic tests. The pattern here — pain that started around your belly button and settled in the lower right, loss of appetite, a wee bit of fever, and the tenderness I found — points quite strongly to your appendix being inflamed. That's called appendicitis. It's very common at your age, and it's definitely not a stomach bug, so I don't want us to sit on it.

Here's the plan:
- You need to go to the hospital emergency department today, and you're well enough to drive or get driven there now. I've organised a referral, and I'd suggest getting a friend or family member to drive you if you can — don't drive yourself through pain.
- Don't eat or drink anything until the hospital team has seen you, just in case they want to take you straight to surgery.
- I've given you 1000 mg of paracetamol for pain; you can take more paracetamol if needed, but avoid ibuprofen until the hospital confirms the diagnosis.

Go straight to the ED even if the pain starts to ease — the pain can ease temporarily even when the appendix is getting worse. And if before you get there the pain suddenly becomes severe, your tummy gets hard, or you feel faint or start vomiting repeatedly, call 000 and stay still.

The ED will do their own bloods, and usually a CT scan, to confirm — I've started a blood test here too but it won't be back today and it shouldn't change what I'm telling you: get seen this afternoon. Do you feel able to get there?
reply: Yeah. I'll go. I just... don't want to be in a hospital. But I'll go.

utterance: That's completely understandable, and you've done the right thing agreeing. It's a small hospital visit with a big payoff — if it's the appendix, you'll be in and out of surgery quickly and home within a day or two. I'd rather you come for nothing than go home and risk it bursting. Off you go, and get someone to drive you.
